rules.title: Mus Rules
rules.subtitle: Official rules and learning guide to play Mus
rules.intro1: Mus is a traditional card game of Basque origin, widely played throughout Spain and parts of Latin America. It is played in pairs (4 players total) using the 40-card Spanish deck. The objective is to reach a set number of points before the opposing pair (usually 30 or 40 points).
rules.intro2: Mus is a traditional card game played in pairs. It is usually played to thirty or forty points, and silent communication (signs) between partners is essential to achieve victory.
rules.lancesIntro: Each hand of Mus consists of 4 consecutive rounds in which players bet tokens (called "amarracos" and "piedras"). The value of the cards from highest to lowest is: King (10 points), Three (10 points), Knight (9 points), Jack (8 points), Seven, Six, Five, Four, Two (1 point), Ace (1 point).
rules.grandeDesc: The pair with the highest value cards wins. First the highest cards of each player are compared, then the second highest, etc. Kings, Threes (in the 8 Kings variant) and Knights are the strongest cards.
rules.chicaDesc: Played in reverse of La Grande: the pair with the lowest value cards wins. Aces and Twos (in the 8 Kings variant) are the best cards for this round.
rules.paresDesc: Round where having cards of the same value is rewarded. Before betting, each player announces if they have pairs. If nobody has any, the round is skipped. The types of pairs from lowest to highest are:
rules.duples: Duples: Two pairs of equal cards or four equal cards.
rules.juegoDesc: The value of the 4 cards is added. If any player adds up to 31 or more, there is "Juego". If nobody reaches it, "Punto" is played. The best game is 31 (called "Joko Nagusia"), followed by 40, 36, 37, 35, 34, 33 and 32. In case of playing Punto, the player who adds up to a value closest to 31 wins (with 30 being the best point).
rules.signsIntro: In Mus it is allowed (and it is a key part of the game) to pass confidential information about your cards to your partner through pre-established gestures or signs. Watch out! If your opponents catch you doing them, they will discover your strategy. Lying with signs is not allowed.
rules.signReyesDesc: Indicates you have two Kings in hand.
rules.signAsesDesc: Indicates you have two Aces in hand.
rules.signMediasDesc: Indicates three cards of the same value.
rules.signDuplesDesc: Indicates you have duples in hand.
rules.sign31Desc: Indicates you have the ideal sum of 31 points for Juego.
rules.signCiegoDesc: Indicates you have no juego (less than 31 points) or you are "blind".
rules.8reyesDesc: It is the most played variant in Biscay and Gipuzkoa. Threes are equivalent to Kings, and Twos are equivalent to Aces. This means there are 8 Kings and 8 Aces in the deck, causing many more hands with high pairs, strong juego and duples, which speeds up and increases the excitement of the game.
rules.4reyesDesc: Threes and Twos are normal numerical cards with their value of 3 and 2 points respectively. In this variant high pairs and 31 hands are much rarer, forcing a more tactical and controlled game of mus.
